chunks: My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) who said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad al-Isfahani, from Suleiman ibn Dawud al-Munqari, from Hafs ibn Ghiyath al-Nakha'i, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Whoever is a traveler should travel on Saturday, for if a stone were to shift from a mountain on Saturday, God would return it to its place.
ai.seo_question: Why is Saturday considered a good day for traveling in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: In al-Khisal, Shaykh al-Saduq records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) emphasizing Saturday as a day of divine stability and protection for travelers. The cosmological metaphor of a stone being restored to its mountain underscores the unique spiritual potency of this day, reflecting the Shia tradition of attributing specific virtues to the days of the week based on prophetic and imamic teachings.
